analysis.title: China: Three things in China
key_insights: China's Q3 real GDP grew 4.5% yoy, slightly above the 4.4% consensus. September activity data were firmer, with industrial production at 5.5% yoy and retail sales and fixed asset investment somewhat better than expected.

Activity data have been notably stronger in quarter-end months (March, June, September, December). GS says this pattern continues to hold, and the 2026 real GDP growth target of 4.5-5% appears on track.

PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng said at the Financial Street Forum that the central bank plans to shift its policy rate from the 7-day reverse repo rate to the overnight reverse repo rate at some point. This continues the modernization of the monetary policy framework, after the narrowing of the interest rate corridor and the introduction of regular overnight reverse repos.

GS expects the switch to the overnight rate next year. It could effectively cut the policy rate by 15bp, from the current 7-day reverse repo rate of 1.4% to the reported overnight reverse repo rate of 1.25%.

Fiscal data show effective tightening this year, contrary to GS's early-year expectation of moderate loosening. In the first nine months, combined general public budget and government managed fund revenues rose 1.4% yoy while expenditures fell 3.5% yoy.

GS's estimated augmented fiscal deficit (AFD) narrowed from 11.0% of GDP in December 2025 to 9.4% in September 2026 on a 12-month moving average basis. GS lowered its 2026 full-year AFD estimate to 10.0% of GDP from 11.5%, while still expecting a notably looser fiscal stance in Q4 given recent policy announcements.
GS names fiscal tightening as the key reason for this year's domestic economic weakness.

Activity strength concentrates in quarter-end months, so non-quarter-end months may be weaker.
